title: fix(channels): fence ingress repair and uncertain writes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A queued plugin Doctor repair could mutate channel ingress after its repair window closed, and ingress writes with unknown native outcomes could be replayed by retry or settlement handling.

## User Impact

Expired Doctor repair writes now roll back. An unknown append, completion, release, or dead-letter outcome remains terminal instead of being retried or acknowledged as a known success. Ordinary transient retries and claim ownership behavior remain intact. There is no schema, configuration, retention, durability, or update protocol change, and no migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now passes its existing live repair authority to the queue's worker admission boundary. The existing worker error classifier guards both write retry loops and the settlement owner. Retaining the rejected settlement prevents the outer dispatch error handler or a later callback from starting another write, while clearing the in-flight marker lets joined shutdown report the failure without spinning. Read-only Doctor inspection retains its noncreating behavior.

Updates continue to permit writes within the active repair section; a queued write whose lease expires refuses at transaction or commit admission under the same owner.

## Evidence

Five negative controls reproduced the missing Doctor commit fence and direct/wrapped unknown-outcome replays. Two additional real drain controls proved that release and dead-letter writes ran twice through outer settlement reentry even after the inner retry guard was fixed. They now run once, retain claim ownership, and joined disposal reports the original unknown failure.

The focused and sibling proof covers 99 distinct cases, including Doctor repair/inspection lifecycle, monitor admission and shutdown, retained ownership, and known transient retry behavior. Final standalone changed-file costs used `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| Test file | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/infra/state-migrations.plugin-doctor-context.test.ts` | 11 passed | 28.161s |
| `src/channels/message/ingress-monitor.admission.test.ts` | 4 passed | 7.747s |
| `src/channels/message/ingress-drain.ownership.test.ts` | 8 passed | 26.290s |

Fresh isolated P0–P2 review is clean on the final source. The full changed check passed in 1488.903s, including production types, all 25 test type graphs, lint, dead-export checks, and guards.

An isolated [published-updater compatibility run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36267688174) passed: published `openclaw@2026.9.4` upgraded to candidate `2026.9.6` with `status: ok`. The `custom-plugin-siblings` scenario loaded the plugin before and after the update, exercised its real Doctor and runtime registrations, and preserved its original source. Canonical build passed in 423.5s, strict packaging in 56.7s, and the update cell in 99.4s. Source hashes matched before and after; candidate tarball SHA256 is `1f6be2b485de9cd52da508459f030188c2135610d13c8a529a4c1671f3568583`.

The two update warnings were expected fixture advisories: preserving an operator-managed plugin and flagging a synthetic plaintext Gateway token. A supplemental source guard initially rejected the receiver's private carrier commit before any build or test; correcting it to verify the complete source tree allowed the successful run. The provider portal timed out after command success; the joined command exit and update receipts independently confirm success. The lease was stopped after the cell finished, and its hosting workflow is marked cancelled. The pass result is established by the joined command exit, update result, canary assertions, and matching source/package receipts; the hosting workflow conclusion alone is not cell proof.

This compatibility cell uses isolated synthetic state and manual restart mode. It complements the exact native Doctor expiry regression; it does not reproduce that race through the published updater or prove a live service restart. Hosted [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36269315128) passed all 125 executed jobs (21 skipped). Its verbose test logs report summed test-case durations of 3.302s for the eight ownership cases, 0.908s for the four admission cases, and 1.376s for the eleven Doctor-context cases. The seven added cases total 2.803s. These are case-duration sums, not standalone file wall times; the table above records measured local file wall times.
